takeaways: Every AI coding tool answers differently because of the harness behind it, and teams can engineer their own harnesses, loops and skills to guide agents toward consistent results.
Reliable AI output needs end-to-end tests, benchmarks for tokens, time and cost, and guardrail gates, while over-engineered harnesses waste context and money.
Keep a human in the loop, share team conventions with the AI as skills, and invest in soft skills and fundamentals, because AI is a tool and not your boss.
hook: AI demos are easy, but AI systems that deliver consistent, trustworthy results take real engineering. This conversation is for developers, tech leads and teams adopting AI coding agents. Alan Buscaglia explains how harnesses, skills, tests, guardrails and a human in the loop turn unpredictable AI into dependable output.
